explanations: terra: Those established عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ are ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, giving the section's idea of remaining in good the stable ground of guidance.

luna: The fire kindled by the hypocrites does light its surroundings, but its light is then taken away: “اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا” and “ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ” contrast with the section's fire-striker that never sparks. | terra: The person kindles a fire, then God takes نُورِهِمْ and leaves them in darkness; the fire succeeds physically but its seekers are left without its light.
luna: Abraham asks for a messenger who will recite, teach, and “يُزَكِّيهِمْ”; this shows purification as a gift mediated to people, alongside the section's account of a person purifying the self.
luna: The messenger's mission includes “وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ,” a direct instance of the same purification root with God and messenger as agents rather than the individual as agent.
terra: The person who asks only for this world has وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ, a seeker left with no portion in the enduring life.
terra: The second petitioner seeks good in both lives and protection from the Fire, supplying the rightly directed search beside 2:200.
terra: أُو۟لَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ answers the section's diminished portion with a share resulting from what these seekers earned.

luna: A deed is likened to a smooth rock covered in soil, which a downpour leaves bare; the visible covering and lost yield parallel a deed that leaves its doer with nothing. | terra: Ostentatious charity is like soil washed from smooth rock, leaving it bare; the givers retain nothing مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟.
terra: Spending for God's pleasure and from inner firmness is like a garden yielding doubled produce, the fruitful reversal of the bare rock in 2:264.
terra: A fruitful garden is struck by a fiery whirlwind when its owner is vulnerable, a concrete image of long labor yielding nothing at the moment it is needed.
terra: Good spent while seeking God's face is for the giver's own self and will be repaid fully, joining the sought object, self-benefit, and an undiminished result.

terra: God holds people to account whether they reveal or conceal what is within their selves; this may bound the section's self-concealment by showing that inward hiding cannot remove its contents from divine knowledge.
terra: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ assigns each self its acquired good and incurred evil, the section's two self-produced shares.
terra: God knows what people hide in their breasts and what they reveal; the link is an indirect boundary on the section's image of suppressing the self rather than the same act.
terra: Those who trade God's covenant and oaths for a small price have no share in the Hereafter, a direct scene of choosing diminution and ending deprived.
terra: Wrongdoers' expenditure is likened to a freezing wind that destroys a crop, so apparent provision and effort leave no harvest.
terra: فَيَنقَلِبُوا خَائِبِينَ depicts the defeated party turning back disappointed, a direct scene of returning without the object sought.
terra: Whoever desires the reward of this world receives from it, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter receives from it; the ayah states the section's two searches in parallel.
terra: مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ identifies the two desired objects amid a battle where disobedience has already changed the outcome.
luna: The messenger sent among believers “وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ”; this repeats the section's purification theme while specifying its communal, prophetic agent.

luna: The verse calls the one removed from the Fire and admitted to the Garden successful, defining success as the final outcome opposite to the wretched fire in the section's cross-references. | terra: Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has attained success, while worldly life is only deceptive enjoyment.
terra: God answers that He does not let the work of any worker be lost, then promises expiation and gardens to those who bore exile and harm.
terra: Patience, mutual steadfastness, watchful constancy, and God-consciousness lead to لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ, giving falah the sustained action suggested by remaining in good.

luna: Those who “يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمْ” are checked by “بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَاءُ”; this sets a boundary on reading 91:9's purification as self-asserted achievement. | terra: Those who يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم are corrected with بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ, distinguishing self-praise from the purification tied to falah.
terra: The ayah calls worldly enjoyment little, the Hereafter better for the God-conscious, and promises they will not be wronged even by a thread-like amount.
terra: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا is reminded that with God are the rewards of both world and Hereafter, correcting a search narrowed to the nearer return.

luna: The command to seek a means toward God and strive, “وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ وَجَاهِدُوا,” ends “لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ”; it states an aim and effort that lead to success. | terra: ٱبْتَغُوا۟ إِلَيْهِ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ وَجَٰهِدُوا۟ ... لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ explicitly connects seeking a way, exertion, and falah.
terra: The person who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs is told that wrongdoers do not attain falah, combining the two failed types quoted in 20:61 and 20:111.
terra: A person made alive and given نُورًا يَمْشِى بِهِ contrasts with one trapped in darkness, reversing the section's dimmed self and lightless hand.
terra: The command to act toward one's position ends with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ, connecting the eventual outcome with the wrongdoing borne by the failed person in 20:111.
terra: وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا makes each self bear the result of its own earning, reinforcing 35:18's self-directed purification.

luna: At the weighing, those whose scales are heavy “هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ”; this makes success a measured outcome, relevant to the section's shrinking or preserved share. | terra: Those whose scales are heavy are هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ; falah is pictured as arriving at judgment with real weight rather than a diminished share.

luna: The light-scaled are said to have lost themselves, “خَسِرُوا أَنفُسَهُم,” the explicit opposite of the successful heavy-scaled in 7:8 and a concrete loss of self. | terra: Those whose scales are light خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُم, a concrete negative counterpart to 7:8 and to the section's person who lowers his own self's portion.
terra: Those who follow ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُ are هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, directly joining the light missing from the failed fire-stick with falah.
terra: God does not alter a favor given to a people until they alter what is in their selves, connecting inward corruption with a diminished provision.
terra: أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ questions satisfaction with the nearer life when its enjoyment is little beside the lasting one.
terra: Earlier peoples enjoyed their خَلَاق, but their deeds became void and they became the losers; the ayah connects a consumed share with wasted work.

luna: The charity is taken “تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا,” cleansing and purifying the giver; this specifies a deed through which the section's tazkiya is realized. | terra: Charity is taken to cleanse and وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا, showing purification and growth enacted through a concrete gift.

terra: Every thirst, fatigue, hunger, and step endured in God's path is recorded as a righteous deed; this concretely proves the section's boundary that fatigue need not be wretchedness or wasted effort.
terra: Fabricating against God or denying His signs ends with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ, restating the section's fabricator who returns deprived.

luna: “إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ” explicitly joins fabricated falsehood to failure, repeating the connection in 20:61. | terra: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ restates with falah vocabulary the section's 20:61 claim that the fabricator خَابَ.
terra: Those who desire worldly life and its adornment are paid their deeds there وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يُبْخَسُونَ, setting up a pursuit fully paid only in the wrong domain.
terra: In the Hereafter those worldly seekers have only the Fire, and وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ makes their labor finally empty.

luna: “فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ” divides people at the final reckoning into wretched and happy, the same opposed outcomes named by the section's root sh-q-w. | terra: فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِىٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ makes the judgment-day division between the wretched and the happy explicit, matching the section's two opposed outcomes.

luna: Immediately after the division into wretched and happy in 11:105, the wretched are assigned to the Fire; the verse gives the first concrete outcome of the section's sh-q-w root. | terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُوا۟ places the wretched group of 11:105 in the Fire, supplying the first outcome of that ayah's division.

luna: The next verse describes their continued stay in the Fire, extending the wretched outcome from 11:106. | terra: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا gives the wretched group a terrible continuance, showing that mere duration differs from the section's falah of remaining in good.

luna: The happy are placed in the Garden and remain there; this completes the contrast introduced by the wretched and happy in 11:105 and makes lasting good concrete. | terra: Opposite those who شَقُوا۟, the happy remain in the Garden and receive عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ, a gift never cut off that realizes lasting good.
terra: Joseph rejects the invited betrayal with إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ, giving wrongdoing a concrete temptation and a failed result.
terra: God does not change a people's condition until they change what is in their own selves, a specific account of inward action producing the attained condition.

luna: In the parable, foam from both floodwater and smelted metal is cast away, while what benefits people remains on earth; this closely stages the section's distinction between lasting good and a fruitless yield. | terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءًۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ distinguishes what vanishes uselessly from what benefits and remains, the section's two results in physical form.

luna: The next verse contrasts those who respond to God and receive the best with those who refuse and face a bad reckoning and Hell; it supplies the moral outcomes after 13:17's image of what remains and what is discarded.

luna: “وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ” directly applies khāba to every defiant tyrant, the same failed outcome named in the section. | terra: وَخَابَ كُلُّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ applies the section's خَابَ to the obstinate tyrant after the messengers seek victory.

luna: After the defiant tyrant has failed in 14:15, the next verse places Hell before him and describes a foul drink, giving that failure a concrete end. | terra: مِّن وَرَآئِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ gives the failed tyrant of 14:15 what lies ahead and begins to specify what his empty-handed end contains.

luna: The following verse depicts him barely swallowing, with death approaching from every side but not arriving; his striving ends in unrelieved affliction. | terra: Death comes to the tyrant from every side وَمَا هُوَ بِمَيِّتٍ, extending his failure into an existence that cannot even reach death.

luna: The deeds of the wrongdoers are “كَرَمَادٍ اشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ,” ashes scattered by wind with no gain from what was earned, an image of effort yielding nothing. | terra: The rejecters' deeds become ashes driven by wind, and لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ makes their earnings unobtainable.
luna: The preceding ayah says the father hides from the people after the news of a daughter; that concealment sets up the literal burial “يَدُسُّهُ” in 16:59.

luna: The dictionary form behind the section's “dassā” is literal concealment: “يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ,” burying the newborn girl in dust; it makes the section's hidden-self image tangible while showing its destructive form. | terra: أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ uses the section's d-s-s/d-s-w word family in its concrete sense of hiding a child in the earth, exposing the violence within the image of burying a self.
terra: The command not to trade God's covenant for a small price says what is with God is better, preparing 16:96's contrast between what perishes and what remains.
terra: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ states directly that one possession runs out while the other remains, clarifying falah as continuance in good.
luna: A believing man or woman who does good is promised a good life and reward according to the best of their work, concretely connecting good action with what the person receives.
terra: Those who fabricate lawful and unlawful against God لَا يُفْلِحُونَ, another concrete meeting of false invention with failed attainment.
terra: إِنْ أَحْسَنتُمْ أَحْسَنتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا makes good and harm return to the acting selves.

luna: The person who seeks the immediate life receives only what is willed for him, while Hell is the end prepared for him; this directly asks what the seeker actually gets. | terra: Whoever seeks ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ receives only what God hastens for whom He wills and then reaches Hell, a precise failed pursuit of the nearer life.

luna: The one who seeks the Hereafter, strives for it with faith, has an effort that is appreciated; this is a specific counterpart to the section's successful search. | terra: Whoever seeks the Hereafter and makes its proper striving has سَعْيُهُم مَّشْكُورًا, the positive pursuit opposed to futile exhaustion.

luna: The following verse says that both groups receive provision from their Lord in this life, qualifying the idea of success by distinguishing immediate provision from the final outcome in 17:18–19. | terra: كُلًّا نُّمِدُّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مِنْ عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَ says both kinds of seeker in 17:18-19 receive worldly supply, while their final results still diverge.
luna: The passage says the Hereafter is greater in rank and distinction than this life, directly extending the near-life versus lasting-good contrast in 87:16–17.
terra: If the cave companions are forced back into their people's religion, وَلَن تُفْلِحُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًا; falah here is enduring fidelity rather than momentary survival.
luna: After his garden is ruined, its owner “يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ” over what he spent; the turned palms make wasted expenditure visible, like the section's empty-handed khāba.
luna: The worldly-life parable grows green, then dries and becomes scattered debris; beside the lasting good deeds of 18:46, it contrasts what vanishes with what remains.

luna: “الْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ” are better and more lasting than worldly adornment, closely echoing the section's gloss of falah as remaining in good. | terra: ٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ are better in reward and hope, uniting lasting good with the seeker's expectation of an outcome.

luna: The question about the greatest losers in deeds introduces people whose effort fails despite their confidence; the next verse supplies the section's specific parallel of a search that yields no good. | terra: هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا asks for the people whose work has produced the greatest loss, directly opening the section's image of strenuous failure.

luna: Their effort has gone astray in worldly life although they think they are doing well, a precise case of striving without attaining the sought good. | terra: ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ ... وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا depicts effort going astray while its doers suppose they are achieving well.

luna: The next verse says their deeds are null and have no weight on the Day of Resurrection, completing the failed effort described in 18:104. | terra: The people whose striving went astray denied their Lord's signs and meeting, so their works became void and have no weight at judgment.
terra: Hell is the recompense for the people of 18:103-105, completing the account of where their seemingly good workmanship actually leads.

luna: Zakariyya says he has never been “شَقِيًّا” in calling on God: here the root means disappointed, a direct reversal of the section's hand left empty. | terra: Zechariah says he has never been بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا: his seeking through prayer has not ended in deprivation, joining the section's search and sh-q-w senses.

luna: Jesus says he was not made “جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا”; the paired tyrant and wretchedness recalls 14:15's tyrant who fails, but here is explicitly denied of Jesus. | terra: Jesus says God did not make him جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا; the pairing of tyrant and wretched directly meets the section's quoted tyrant who خَابَ in 14:15.
terra: Abraham hopes not to be بِدُعَاءِ رَبِّى شَقِيًّا, again using sh-q-w for a petitioner's feared failure to obtain what he seeks.
terra: ٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ are better in reward and return, a repeated formulation of the good that remains and yields the better end.

luna: The Qur'an was not sent “لِتَشْقَىٰ”; this negated use of the section's sh-q-w root distinguishes divine reminder from the toil that ends in wretchedness. | terra: مَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰ uses the section's sh-q-w word for hardship and explicitly denies that the revelation was sent to exhaust its recipient.
luna: The continuation calls the Qur'an “تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ,” specifying the fearful recipient of the reminder after 20:2 denies that it was sent to cause distress.
terra: Moses sees a fire and hopes to bring a قَبَسٍ or find guidance at it, a seeker approaching light with a stated object.
terra: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ shows that Moses' fire-search does reach something: at arrival he receives the divine call.

luna: Moses warns the magicians that “وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ افْتَرَىٰ”; the same kh-y-b verb marks false invention as an effort that ends empty. | terra: Moses' warning وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ makes fabrication a pursuit whose maker returns deprived, exactly the section's خَابَ result.
terra: Pharaoh's magicians claim وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ; their falah means gaining worldly ascendancy, a pointed rival sense to remaining in moral good.
luna: In the same contest, “لَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ” says the magician does not prosper; its outcome repeats the failure tied to falsehood in 20:61.
terra: The criminal in Hell لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ exactly repeats 87:13's result for the most wretched person.

luna: The gardens of Eden, abiding forever, are “جَزَاءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ”; this directly joins purification to an enduring good outcome. | terra: Eternal gardens are called جَزَاءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ, giving purification the lasting good that the section hears in falah.

luna: “وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا” repeats the section's khāba formula for one who carries wrongdoing and fails. | terra: وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا gives the section's empty-handed outcome to the person who arrives at judgment carrying wrongdoing.

luna: After 20:111 says the bearer of wrongdoing has failed, this verse gives the opposite case: a believer doing good need fear neither injustice nor loss. | terra: The righteous believer need not fear ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا, an explicit protection from injustice or diminution opposite the section's self whose share is made small.

luna: God warns Adam that Satan must not expel the pair from the Garden “فَتَشْقَىٰ”; the section's sh-q-w root here names the toil or hardship of the lost garden. | terra: Adam is warned that expulsion from the garden will leave him فَتَشْقَىٰ, illustrating the section's secondary sense of sh-q-w as toil and hardship.
luna: The next ayah describes the Garden's protection from hunger and nakedness, “أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ,” making concrete the deprivation behind the warning in 20:117.
luna: Its continuation adds no thirst or sun exposure, “لَا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ”; these bodily hardships spell out the toil contrasted with the Garden.

luna: After the descent from the Garden, one who follows God's guidance “فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ”; guidance avoids the very wretchedness named in the section. | terra: فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ promises that following divine guidance prevents both losing the way and ending in wretchedness.
luna: The next ayah gives the counter-outcome for turning from remembrance: “مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا,” a constricted life, linking avoidance to a diminished share.
terra: The passing bloom of worldly life is set against رِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ, identifying the better and more lasting provision.
terra: The command to persevere in prayer is joined to نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ and وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ, connecting sustained effort, provision, and final outcome.
terra: For the believer who does righteous deeds there is no rejection of striving—فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ—and it is recorded, directly reversing futile effort.
terra: The person who worships on an edge turns back under trial and خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةَ, a pursuit that loses both the near and lasting goods.

luna: “قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ” gives the successful group whose qualities, including doing zakat in 23:4, make the section's success-through-purification concrete. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ repeats the section's emphatic قَدْ أَفْلَحَ construction and opens a concrete account of those who attain the good sought.
luna: The successful believers are described as “لِلزَّكَاةِ فَاعِلُونَ”; the root of purification is made an actual deed within their profile.
terra: أُو۟لَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثُونَ begins to specify what the successful believers of 23:1 actually receive.
terra: ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ defines their attainment as inheriting Paradise and remaining there, the section's lexical account of falah made scene.
terra: Heavy scales again identify هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, placing falah in the judgment scene that soon contains the confession of wretchedness in 23:106.
terra: Light scales mean خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ, directly staging the self as the thing the failed person has lost.
terra: Fire scorches the faces of those whose light scales meant loss of self, specifying the bodily consequence before their confession in 23:106.
terra: The condemned are asked whether God's signs were recited and rejected; their failure to receive the reminder explains the wretchedness confessed next.

luna: The condemned say “غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا”; wretchedness has overcome them, giving the section's “ashqa” a first-person account of failure. | terra: The condemned confess رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا; wretchedness has overcome them and brought their striving to its failed end.

luna: After confessing that their wretchedness overcame them in 23:106, the people ask to be taken out of the Fire so they can do good; the desired return is now unavailable. | terra: Immediately after confessing their wretchedness, the condemned ask to be taken out and promise righteousness if returned; even their new search is now too late.

luna: They are told to remain there in humiliation and not speak, completing the failed plea of 23:107. | terra: ٱخْسَـُٔوا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تُكَلِّمُونِ refuses that request, leaving the failed seekers without the exit they seek.
terra: A group of believers had prayed for forgiveness and mercy, introducing the people whose patient seeking receives the contrary result in 23:111.
terra: The condemned mocked those petitioners until mockery made them forget God's remembrance, showing how their own conduct obscured the self.
terra: إِنِّى جَزَيْتُهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ gives patient believers attained victory opposite the confessing wretched group.

luna: The verse says that without God's grace none would be purified and that “اللَّهَ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَاءُ”; this makes divine agency a boundary around the section's success through purification. | terra: مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا without God's grace places divine enabling around the section's human act of purifying the self.
terra: Lowering the gaze and guarding chastity is ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ, a specific practice by which a self becomes purer.
terra: The command to all believers to turn back to God ends لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ, presenting repentance as a directed course toward falah.
luna: The lamp's oil “يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ,” a specific image of near self-emitting light opposite the hand left without a spark.

luna: The thirsty person expects water in a mirage but “إِذَا جَاءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئًا”; this is a specific search that reaches its object and finds nothing, like the section's khāba. | terra: A thirsty person pursues a mirage, then لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْـًٔا: this is the section's empty-handed seeker rendered as a complete Quranic scene.

luna: In layered darkness a person can hardly see his hand, and “مَن لَّمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُ مِن نُّورٍ”; this parallels the section's hand left without light. | terra: The following layered darkness ends وَمَن لَّمْ يَجْعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ, matching the section's hand left without a spark or light.
terra: Deeds are turned هَبَآءً مَّنثُورًا, a visible counterpart to exertion that yields no retained good.
terra: Moses sees a fire and promises either news or بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ, repeating the concrete search for a usable flame.
terra: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ makes arrival at the fire yield a call and blessing, more than the ember initially sought.
terra: Moses hopes to return from the distant fire with news or جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ, another direct fire-seeking scene.
terra: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ completes the search: reaching the fire becomes the site of revelation.
terra: Moses says God knows who receives the good final home and that wrongdoers do not attain falah, joining moral burden to final result.
terra: Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment, while مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ identifies the better and more lasting object.

luna: Repentance, faith, and good work are followed by hope of being “مِنَ الْمُفْلِحِينَ”; this names a concrete route to the success the section ties to purification. | terra: Repentance, belief, and righteous action make a person likely to be among ٱلْمُفْلِحِينَ, specifying a repaired course for the self.
terra: وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ directs the seeker's resources toward the enduring home while retaining a proper worldly share.
terra: Those who desire worldly life see Qarun's display and wish for his portion, establishing the mistaken search corrected in 28:82.
terra: People of knowledge answer that God's reward is better for belief and righteous action, naming the better object of pursuit.
terra: The earth swallows Qarun and his home, making the admired worldly attainment vanish before the wishers' eyes.
terra: People who had wished for Qarun's place discover that provision is measured by God and conclude لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ, a corrected worldly search ending in a falah judgment.
terra: The lasting home is for those who do not seek عُلُوًّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ; this corrects the magicians' claim in 20:64 that success belongs to whoever rises highest.
luna: “وَمَن يُجَاهِدُ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَاهِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ” says striving accrues to the striver, a close parallel to the section's account of what each self gains.
terra: Those who strive for God are promised guidance into His ways, showing exertion that opens a path rather than ending in exhausted deprivation.
terra: Those who يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ are called ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ, so the object consciously sought and the attainment of falah meet in one ayah.
terra: Charity given while seeking God's face makes its givers ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ, an enlarged return opposite the section's self whose share is diminished.
terra: The repeated pairing عَلَىٰ هُدًى ... هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ again pictures falah as continuance upon guidance.

luna: The cited “وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِ” says purification benefits the purifier; the same ayah says no burdened soul can transfer its load, defining what each person receives. | terra: وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِ makes purification accrue to one's own self, directly answering the section's self whose share is enlarged or diminished.

luna: God makes fire from a green tree “فَإِذَا أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ,” a successful ignition opposite to the “hayyāb” stick that gives no spark. | terra: God makes fire from ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ so that people kindle from it, a concrete reversal of the section's stick that yields no spark.
terra: إِنَّ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ makes the self itself the decisive loss on judgment day.
terra: مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِۦ وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا repeats the precise self-benefit and self-harm relation developed in the section.
terra: The two seekers desire different harvests; the seeker of the world receives some of it but has no نَصِيبٍ in the Hereafter, exactly the section's diminished share.
terra: Whatever people receive is only worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ for believers who trust Him.

luna: This verse states that whoever does good does it “فَلِنَفْسِهِ” and whoever does evil does it against himself, specifying the personal share at stake in the section. | terra: The same formula makes righteous action accrue to one's own self and evil fall against it before all return to their Lord.
terra: The command to cast كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ into Hell supplies a repeated obstinate figure and destination for the عَنِيد whose failure the section quotes from 14:15.
luna: The verse states that wrongdoers are recompensed for their deeds and good-doers receive the best; it grounds the purification warning of 53:32 in the section's two different outcomes.

luna: “فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ” warns against claiming one's own purity, qualifying the section's language of purifying the self with God's knowledge of who is truly mindful. | terra: فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ draws a boundary between actually purifying the self and claiming purity for oneself; God best knows who is mindful.
luna: The passage singles out one who turns away; this gives a concrete act of avoidance alongside the section's account of the ashqa who avoids a reminder.
luna: That person gives a little and then withholds, a specific image of the stinginess opposite the giving and purification in 92:18 and the self-sufficient course in 92:8.

luna: “وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ” ties what a person receives to his own striving, directly clarifying the section's two searches. | terra: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ makes what a person obtains answer directly to what the person strove for.

luna: The continuation says “وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ”; the seeker's own effort is brought into view, not lost from the account. | terra: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُۥ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ promises that the striving itself will be brought into view rather than disappear unnoticed.

luna: The next verse promises “ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَىٰ,” completing the sequence from striving to its full result. | terra: ثُمَّ يُجْزَىٰهُ ٱلْجَزَاءَ ٱلْأَوْفَىٰ completes the sequence with full recompense, the opposite of a shrunken share.

luna: The question “أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ” names fire that people kindle, directly reversing the section's fire-making attempt that yields no spark. | terra: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى تُورُونَ addresses people about the fire they kindle, the successful act reversed in the section's non-sparking stick.

luna: The next ayah asks who created the fire's tree, “أَأَنتُمْ أَنشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا,” extending the scene from kindling to the source of its fuel. | terra: The question whether humans produced شَجَرَتَهَا locates the kindled fire in its tree, the material counterpart to the section's fire-stick.

luna: The fire is made “تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ,” a reminder and provision for travelers, giving the kindled fire a useful yield unlike the section's failed strike. | terra: God makes that fire تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَٰعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ: unlike the useless stick, it gives reminder and provision to travelers.
terra: Believing men and women have their light running before them; this is the attained light that the hypocrites of 57:13 seek only after it is inaccessible.
terra: Hypocrites ask believers for light and are told فَٱلْتَمِسُوا۟ نُورًا behind them; their too-late search for light ends at a barrier.
terra: The failed seekers of light are told that they tempted their own selves, waited, doubted, and were deceived by wishes; the ayah locates their dark result in self-directed acts.
terra: No ransom is accepted from the failed light-seekers and the Fire becomes their refuge, completing the barred search of 57:13-14.
terra: Worldly life is pictured as rain-grown vegetation that impresses, withers, yellows, and becomes debris, a concrete account of the sought good that does not remain.
terra: سَابِقُوٓا۟ directs a race toward forgiveness and a garden, turning the enduring result into an explicitly pursued goal.
terra: This single ayah joins faith written in hearts, gardens in which believers remain, God's pleasure, and the verdict that God's party are ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ.

luna: Those “يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ” are called successful; guarding the self from its grasping disposition contrasts with the section's soul whose share is diminished. | terra: وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ locates the obstacle and the rescue within the self, as this section does.

luna: Each soul is told to look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow and to fear God; this makes the section's question of what each seeker gains an explicit self-accounting. | terra: وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ calls each self to inspect what it has sent ahead, immediately before 59:19's self-forgetting failure.

luna: Those who forget God are made to forget themselves, a direct image of the self-neglect that the section calls dimming and diminishing the soul. | terra: Those who forget God are made to forget أَنفُسَهُمْ, a direct inner parallel to suppressing and losing one's own self.
terra: فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓا۟ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ makes an initial self-chosen deviation end in further distortion of the heart.
luna: The unlettered are taught and purified by the messenger, “وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ”; the verse supplies the same root in a communal form, distinct from the individual's self-purification in 91:9.

luna: After prayer, people are told to seek God's bounty and remember Him “لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ”; seeking, effort, and the desired success are stated together. | terra: فَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ ... لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ joins seeking provision, remembering God, and attaining falah.

luna: This verse again links success to being protected from “شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ”; it makes the soul's disposition and its outcome explicit, as in the section's self that is purified or suppressed. | terra: The repeated formula about being guarded from شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ and becoming ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ again makes treatment of one's self determine the attained result.
terra: Believers ask رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا after sincere repentance, a successful orientation toward the light absent from the section's failed hand.
terra: On the day of presentation no hidden thing remains hidden; this may reverse the buried-self image, though the ayah concerns exposure at judgment rather than self-purification.
terra: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ repeats the preference for the immediate life that marks the failed trajectory in 87:16 and 17:18.
terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ states what is abandoned when the immediate life becomes the sought object.
luna: The righteous say they feed others only for God's face and seek neither repayment nor thanks, a close parallel to 92:19–20's account of giving without seeking a return from people.

luna: The righteous are told that their effort has been appreciated as their reward; this states the successful return to effort that the section contrasts with wasted toil. | terra: وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَّشْكُورًا tells the people of Paradise that their striving was appreciated, a direct counter-image to effort ending fruitless.
terra: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَآءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا gives the same pursuit its neglected consequence.
luna: Hellfire throws “شَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ,” an abundance of sparks that reverses the section's “hayyāb,” the striker that produces none.
luna: The next ayah compares the sparks to “جِمَالَتٌ صُفْرٌ,” extending their scale and abundance against the sparkless striker.

luna: Moses asks Pharaoh “هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ”; the same purification verb is an invitation to the transgressor, making purification a chosen response to wrongdoing. | terra: Moses asks Pharaoh هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ, presenting purification as a path Pharaoh may choose rather than the burying of his self.

luna: The next verse offers guidance to the Lord and fear of Him, “وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ,” completing the invitation to purify in 79:18. | terra: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ joins guidance toward the Lord with fear, the same receptive stance as 87:10.
terra: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مَا سَعَىٰ places remembered striving before the final two-way division.
terra: وَبُرِّزَتِ ٱلْجَحِيمُ لِمَن يَرَىٰ brings the result into sight between remembering one's striving and the division of the two seekers.
terra: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ identifies transgression as the first course whose result follows.
terra: وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats 87:16's preference for the nearer life as the failed seeker's choice.
terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ gives that preference its attained destination.

luna: The one who “نَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ” restrains the self from desire, a specific opposite to dimming or debasing the self in 91:10. | terra: The other person fears standing before the Lord and restrains ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ, treating the self in the opposite way from burying it under desire.

luna: The next verse names that restrained person's refuge as the Garden, completing the opposed outcome to the section's failed, diminished self. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ supplies the lasting destination of the disciplined self.

luna: The blind man who comes may “يَزَّكَّىٰ”; the section's purification is joined to a seeker who arrives for a reminder. | terra: لَعَلَّهُۥ يَزَّكَّىٰ presents purification as the possible outcome for the blind seeker who has come for instruction.

luna: The next verse says he may remember and benefit from the reminder, “أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَىٰ,” joining purification to the section's rememberer who fears. | terra: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ joins remembrance and benefit exactly as the reminder passage in 87:9-10 does.

luna: The counterfigure “مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ” considers himself self-sufficient; this anticipates the section's failed, self-diminishing course and the contrast in 92:8. | terra: أَمَّا مَنِ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ identifies the self-sufficient person who receives attention, the contrary figure to the fearful seeker who comes striving.

luna: The speaker gives attention to that self-sufficient man, “فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ,” while the seeker in 80:8–9 is the one who comes striving and fearing. | terra: فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ records attention being directed to the self-sufficient listener, completing the interpersonal reversal exposed by 80:8-10.

luna: “If he does not purify himself” (“أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ”) is set against the eager seeker; it makes the failure to purify an explicit boundary, not a lack of opportunity. | terra: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ makes the self-sufficient listener's failure to purify himself his own outcome.

luna: The other person “جَاءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ,” comes striving; this directly stages the search and effort in the section's image. | terra: وَأَمَّا مَن جَآءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ makes the receptive person literally come striving, a concrete seeker within the reminder scene.
luna: He also “وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ,” matching the fearful recipient of reminder in 87:10. | terra: وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ gives that striver the fear that characterizes the one who remembers in 87:10.

luna: The striving, fearful seeker is turned away from, “فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ”; this reverses the welcome given to the self-sufficient figure in 80:5–6 and echoes the avoided reminder in 87:11. | terra: فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ records the seeker being overlooked, sharpening the passage's question of who receives the reminder.
terra: The buried girl is brought forward and questioned; this may echo the section's literalized idea of a buried self, though the ayah concerns a murdered child rather than inward concealment.
terra: بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ exposes the guilt behind literal burial; the link to burying one's own self is analogical and the actors differ.

luna: “رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم” pictures what people earned as a rusting cover over their hearts, an inward darkening that parallels the section's self made dim by suppression. | terra: بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ shows a person's own earnings coating and dimming the heart, close to the section's self made obscure by its possessor.
terra: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ makes every human a laboring seeker who will meet the Lord and the result of that labor.
terra: Receiving the record in the right hand begins the favorable result for the laborer who must meet his Lord in 84:6.
terra: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا gives the right-hand recipient an easy accounting, the favorable result of the universal labor in 84:6.
terra: وَيَنقَلِبُ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِۦ مَسْرُورًا makes that seeker return joyfully, opposite the disappointed return captured by خَائِبِينَ in 3:127.
terra: Receiving the record from behind the back begins the contrary result for the same universal labor described in 84:6.
terra: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوا۟ ثُبُورًا shows the unsuccessful laborer calling for destruction when the result is received.
terra: وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا completes that laborer's result in a blaze, paralleling the exhausted faces of 88:3-4.
terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ is the promise of ease immediately before the command to remind, anticipating the two courses toward ease and hardship in Surah 92.

luna: “فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَىٰ” sets up the division the section quotes in 87:10–11: reminder benefits one who fears, while the most wretched avoids it. | terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ is the command that creates the reminder scene divided between the fearful hearer and the avoider in 87:10-11.

luna: The section's remembered one who fears is named here: “سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ”; fear makes the addressee receptive to the reminder. | terra: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ identifies the receptive seeker as the one who fears and takes the reminder, the positive half of the section's quoted division.

luna: The section's “ashqa” avoids the reminder here, “وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَىٰ,” the opposite response to the fearful rememberer of 87:10. | terra: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى names the most wretched as the one who actively avoids the reminder, the negative seeker described in the section.

luna: The next ayah gives the consequence of the “ashqa” who avoids the reminder in 87:11: he enters “النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ”; the section's link between wretchedness and a failed end gains its outcome. | terra: ٱلَّذِى يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ gives the most wretched person's avoidance in 87:11 its fiery result.

luna: The continuation after the great fire of 87:12 says its inhabitants neither die nor live, completing the lasting consequence for the ashqa who avoids reminder. | terra: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ makes failed striving end in a state that is neither death nor life, completing the consequence begun in 87:11-12.

luna: The section reads 91:9's “aflaha” as lasting in good through purification; 87:14 repeats the pairing directly: “قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ.” | terra: The exact parallel قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ joins the section's two positive terms: attaining falah and purifying oneself.

luna: After the purified one in 87:14, “وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ” shows remembering God and prayer as the next concrete response associated with that success. | terra: وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِۦ فَصَلَّىٰ supplies remembrance and prayer as the acts accompanying the purification and falah of 87:14.

luna: The people “تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا” choose the near life, a specific counterpoint to the section's reading of success as remaining in good. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا identifies preference for the nearer life as the rival pursuit immediately after the falah statement.

luna: “الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ” states that the better good endures, closely matching the section's lexical gloss of falah as remaining in good. | terra: وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ makes the better object also the one that remains, sharpening the section's definition of falah as remaining in good.
terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَٰشِعَةٌ introduces the abased faces whose next description is laboring and exhausted; its own contribution is their final humiliation.

luna: “عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ” portrays faces laboring and exhausted, closely matching the section's dictionary note that wretchedness is a form of toil. | terra: عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ pictures faces whose labor has only exhausted them, the closest nonlexical parallel to the section's most strenuous person ending depleted.

luna: The exhausted faces in 88:3 “تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً”; this gives their toil the ruinous destination described in the section's account of the ashqa. | terra: تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً gives the exhausted labor of 88:3 its destination in fire.

luna: The same scene continues with drink from “عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ,” an affliction after the exhausted labor of 88:3. | terra: The exhausted faces are made to drink from a boiling spring, specifying what their labor has obtained.

luna: Their food is only “مِن ضَرِيعٍ,” continuing the deprivation that makes this an image of effort ending without benefit. | terra: Their only food is bitter thorn, another concrete yield of labor that ended in wretchedness.

luna: That food “لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِن جُوعٍ”; the laboring person's provision does not satisfy, a concrete empty return. | terra: لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِن جُوعٍ makes that food neither nourish nor relieve hunger, an exact image of receiving something that supplies no good.

luna: The next group has “وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاعِمَةٌ,” a direct opposite to the exhausted faces of 88:3. | terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاعِمَةٌ opens the opposite judgment scene to the abased, exhausted faces of 88:2-3.

luna: Their state is “لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ,” satisfied with its endeavor, a sharp reversal of the section's labor whose outcome is failure. | terra: لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ reverses the fruitless labor of 88:3: these faces are satisfied with the result of their striving.

luna: The satisfied group's destination is “جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ,” completing the contrast between spent labor and a good attained. | terra: فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ gives the satisfied striving of 88:9 its lasting destination.
luna: The “tranquil soul” is a clear counter-image to the section's dimmed and diminished self.
luna: The tranquil soul returns to its Lord both pleased and pleasing, giving the purified self a specific satisfied end.
luna: The next verse invites that soul among God's servants, continuing its welcome after the return in 89:28.
luna: The passage ends by admitting the soul to the Garden, the lasting good that contrasts with the section's failed outcome.
terra: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِى كَبَدٍ makes toil a general human condition, supporting the section's explicit boundary that not every fatigue is wretchedness.

luna: “إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ” explicitly divides human endeavors; this is the two searches whose different outcomes the section describes. | terra: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ announces divergent strivings, an exact structural parallel to the section's two searches and their different ends.

luna: The good course begins with giving and God-consciousness, “أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ,” concrete deeds leading toward the section's successful outcome. | terra: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ gives generosity and God-consciousness as the first acts on the striving that is eased toward ease in 92:7.

luna: The good course also affirms “الْحُسْنَىٰ”; that trust in the good corresponds to the section's one who reaches and remains in good. | terra: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ supplies affirmation of the best promise as the positive seeker's orientation before the result in 92:7.

luna: “فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ” names the eased outcome of that course, a specific result for one of the divergent endeavors in 92:4. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ gives the generous, God-fearing believer's pursuit a course toward ease.

luna: The counter-course is “بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ,” withholding and acting self-sufficient; it illuminates the section's self whose share is made small. | terra: وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ names stinginess and imagined self-sufficiency as the acts on the striving eased toward hardship in 92:10.

luna: “وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ” makes denial of the good the opposite of the successful, purified course. | terra: وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ gives denial of the best promise as the failed seeker's orientation before the result in 92:10.

luna: The other course is eased toward “الْعُسْرَىٰ,” an explicit adverse result for the seeker who withholds and denies. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ gives the denying, self-sufficient person's pursuit a course toward hardship, the section's labor that ends in depletion.

luna: The following verse says “مَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ” when he falls; wealth cannot deliver the seeker from the failed end described in 92:8–10. | terra: وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ shows the failed seeker discovering that accumulated wealth supplies nothing at the fall.

luna: “نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ” is the fire warned of immediately before 92:15 identifies the most wretched as its entrant, joining that root to a concrete end. | terra: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ introduces the blaze into which 92:15 places the most wretched.

luna: The cited “الْأَشْقَىٰ” enters the blazing fire; it repeats the section's root for the most wretched and connects it to the failed outcome. | terra: لَا يَصْلَىٰهَا إِلَّا ٱلْأَشْقَى repeats the section's superlative ٱلْأَشْقَى and gives that person's final destination.

luna: “كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ” describes denial and turning away, a concrete counterpart to the avoider of the reminder in 87:11. | terra: ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ defines the most wretched of 92:15 by denial and turning away, matching the avoider of the reminder in 87:11.

luna: “The most God-fearing” is kept away from the fire in “وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَىٰ,” the explicit opposite of the ashqa in 92:15. | terra: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَتْقَى reverses 92:15: the most God-fearing is kept away from the fire entered by the most wretched.

luna: “يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ” directly joins giving to purification, matching the section's successful self-purification. | terra: ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُۥ يَتَزَكَّىٰ places self-purification on the opposite trajectory from the most wretched person's fire.

luna: The purifier “لَا يُرِيدُ جَزَاءً” from anyone; this clarifies the self-directed purification in 35:18 that the section cites. | terra: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰ clarifies that the purified giver's expenditure is not repayment of a human favor, preparing 92:20's sole sought object.

luna: His aim is “ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ,” giving the searcher in this passage a stated object of pursuit. | terra: إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ states the purified giver's sought object: the face of his Lord Most High.

luna: “وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ” supplies the sought one's final satisfaction, a concrete counterpart to reaching the desired in the section's gloss of aflaha. | terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ closes that directed search with attainment and satisfaction rather than an empty hand.
terra: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ commands renewed exertion, a positive case of tiring effort rather than the futile labor attached to wretchedness.
terra: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب directs desire to its true object, making the positive exertion of 94:7 a purposeful search.
terra: Those who fear their Lord receive gardens in which they remain forever and mutual pleasure with God, extending the fearful recipient of 87:10 into a lasting result.
terra: فَٱلْمُورِيَٰتِ قَدْحًا stages successful striking that throws sparks, directly illuminating the section's dictionary image of a qadh that is rubbed but will not spark.
terra: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ repeats the heavy-scale side of the judgment image that associates an undiminished share with success.
terra: فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ gives the person of heavy scales a satisfying life, the good attained and retained.
terra: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ repeats the light-scale side, concretizing the section's self whose portion has been made small.
terra: فَأُمُّهُۥ هَاوِيَةٌ gives the light-scale person an abyss as the destination reached.
terra: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا هِيَهْ holds open the identity of that abyss before the next ayah names it.
terra: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ identifies the abyss reached by the person of light scales as a blazing fire.
terra: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ says acquired wealth and earnings avail nothing, close to the fruitless accumulation of 92:11.
terra: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ gives the unavailing earnings of 111:2 their fiery outcome.
